fieldValues.title: Visual editing is chosen per editor
fieldValues.decision_question: Where may a visual text editor be used, given that SRS deliberately uses types and fields rather than rich text to hold structure?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-06 (vignette 19964824): elsewhere we do not use rich text because we want to maintain the data structure; SRS types and fields mean we do not need it, and markdown is only for simple text. 'The essay currently only offers paragraph types. This is a different kind of context and a different user profile.' Precedent consulted: this vignette; 40f62bfd (the essay editor preserves human agency for owning meaning as individuals); decision 82fbca88 (in the essay editor agents never write essay text); ADR-001 (srs-web holds no semantics); capability layering. Placement: the editor group's log, domain Evidence-backed writing.
fieldValues.friction: Without a stated boundary, a visual editor in one editor reads as a move to rich text everywhere, or as a reversal of the structured approach, and the next editor would inherit it by default.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Each editor chooses for its own user profile, and structure stays in types and fields (recommended). For: states what the owner described; keeps structure where it is; leaves each editor free. Against: two editing behaviours to maintain across the product.
B. Essay editor only, as a named exception. For: tightest. Against: names no reason, so the next case has nothing to apply.
C. Offer visual editing for every markdown field. For: one behaviour everywhere. Against: invites formatting into fields where a type should carry the structure, which is the thing the owner wants to avoid.
D. No visual editing anywhere. For: one mechanism, no dependency. Against: leaves the essay's writer facing raw markdown.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Keep the data structure authoritative where types exist; serve the writer the essay is for; do not set a precedent by accident.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Each editor chooses visual text editing for its own user profile, never as a substitute for structured types.
fieldValues.rationale: The choice follows from who is writing and what the editor offers: where types exist, they carry the structure; where a writer has only paragraphs, the surface can serve the writing. Stating the reason makes it testable at the next editor.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A second editor asks for visual editing, or writers in the essay editor start using formatting to fake structure a type should carry.
